minutes.headline: PACC covers the studio move, a costly new Castis server purchase, and a warrant repayment mix-up with the town.
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee reviewed the studio relocation (cameras still need wiring, no dedicated storage room secured), a planned FY27 purchase of a new Castis server after reviewing pricing options, and staffing changes including a new videographer and a resignation that was already backfilled. The committee also discussed a warrant that had confused the town's finance office over a budget line-item repayment, deferring resolution to after the meeting, and voted to adjourn after a brief discussion about normalizing and publishing committee policies online.

what_happened.line: The committee is planning a costly server replacement at the start of FY27, calling the current unit end of life after nine years.
The town's finance office flagged confusion over a warrant the committee submitted, tied to a budget-line repayment not yet assigned to a specific line.
Studio relocation continues, with cameras still needing wiring and no dedicated storage room secured.
A new videographer was already in place before the prior one resigned, so the position did not go vacant.
The committee set its next meeting for November 3rd and will take up normalizing and posting its policies then.

why_it_matters: A major equipment purchase planned for FY27 will show up in the committee's budget request and its enterprise fund balance.

An unresolved repayment tied to a prior annual town meeting appropriation is a loose end between the committee and the town's finance office that residents may see resurface in a warrant or budget line.
The unfinished studio move affects when and where public meetings and programs, including town meeting coverage, can be recorded.
